Class GTNetProtocolLimits

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetProtocolLimits
@Component public class GTNetProtocolLimits extends Object
The bounds an inbound GTNet message must respect before it is persisted, budgeted or dispatched.

The database carries hard bounds of its own — gt_net_message.message is varchar(1000), gt_net_message_param.param_name is varchar(32) and param_value is varchar(255) — but reaching them produces a DataException and an HTTP 500 rather than a protocol rejection the peer can read. These limits are checked first so that an over-sized or malformed envelope is answered with GNetCoreMessageCode.GT_NET_ERROR_S and a stable errorMsgCode.

The values are Spring properties rather than globalparameters rows: they are protocol constants of the library, not something an administrator tunes per instance. The property names are dotted, so they are bound individually with Value instead of through @ConfigurationProperties, whose relaxed binding would read g.gnet.max.body.bytes as a nested object graph.

    • GTNetProtocolLimits

      public GTNetProtocolLimits(@Value("${g.gnet.max.body.bytes:4194304}") int maxBodyBytes, @Value("${g.gnet.max.params:32}") int maxParams, @Value("${g.gnet.max.payload.bytes:2097152}") int maxPayloadBytes, @Value("${g.gnet.max.clock.skew.minutes:5}") int maxClockSkewMinutes, @Value("${g.gnet.token.overlap.days:7}") int tokenOverlapDays)
      Binds the five limits. The property names are dotted, so each is bound individually with Value rather than through @ConfigurationProperties, whose relaxed binding would read g.gnet.max.body.bytes as a nested object graph. Constructor injection keeps the bean constructible in a plain unit test.
      Parameters:
      maxBodyBytes - outer bound on the JSON request body
      maxParams - maximum number of envelope parameters
      maxPayloadBytes - maximum serialized payload size
      maxClockSkewMinutes - accepted deviation of the envelope timestamp from the local clock
      tokenOverlapDays - how long a replaced inbound token stays acceptable
